# Job Chapter 32 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 428r–428v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_032_page_001.jpg, JOB_032_page_002.jpg

---

**1** So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

**2** Then the anger of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned. His anger burned against Job because he justified himself rather than God.

**3** His anger burned also against his three friends because they had found no answer, although they had declared Job to be in the wrong.

**4** Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because they were older than he.

**5** And when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his anger was kindled.

**6** And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: "I am young in years, and you are aged; therefore I was timid and afraid to declare my opinion to you.

**7** I said, 'Let days speak, and many years teach wisdom.'

**8** But it is the spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.

**9** It is not only the great who are wise, nor only the aged who understand what is right.

**10** Therefore I say, 'Listen to me; let me also declare my opinion.'

**11** Behold, I waited for your words; I listened for your wise arguments, while you searched for what to say.

**12** I gave you my attention, and behold, there was none among you who refuted Job or answered his words.

**13** Beware of saying, 'We have found wisdom; God may refute him, not a man.'

**14** He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.

**15** They are dismayed; they answer no more; they have not a word to say.

**16** And shall I wait, because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?

**17** I also will answer with my share; I also will declare my opinion.

**18** For I am full of words; the spirit within me constrains me.

**19** Behold, my stomach is like wine that has no vent; like new wineskins ready to burst.

**20** I must speak, that I may find relief; I must open my lips and answer.

**21** I will not show partiality to any man, nor will I flatter anyone,

**22** for I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon take me away."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**The narrative frame (vv.1-5):** For the first time since chapter 2, the narrator speaks in prose. This signals a major structural shift — the three-friend dialogue cycle is over, and a new voice enters. The narrator's emphasis on Elihu's anger (mentioned four times in five verses) is striking.

**v.2 — Elihu's anger:** The word *charah* ("burned") is used four times in vv.2-5. Elihu is angry at Job for self-justification and at the friends for failing to answer. He positions himself as the solution to both failures.

**v.8 — Democratic inspiration:** Elihu's claim that wisdom comes from God's spirit rather than from age is theologically important — it challenges the wisdom tradition's equation of age with wisdom. But the irony is that Elihu will prove no more successful than the friends.

**v.19 — The wineskin image:** The metaphor is apt but also reveals Elihu's self-regard. He is bursting to speak not because he has the answer but because he cannot contain himself. The reader is invited to be skeptical.

*— LOGOS*
